As against this the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party submits that the order under review itself is illegal as before passing that order no caution was exercised by the learned Munsif. He relied on a decision reported in 23 D.L.R. 461, (Dacca WASA and another Vs. Roushan Ara Begum and ors.) where it has been held "Clause (c) of rule 4 of Order 26 of the Code of Civil Procedure is a sort of exception to the general rule as embodied in rule I of the said Order as to the persons who, though living within the jurisdiction of the court, may be examined on commission and such an exception should be strictly construed." The learned Advocate for the opposite party then relied on another decision reported in 28 D.L.R. 17 (S.M. Moazzem Hossain Vs. Md. Anwar and others) wherein it has been held that "Issue of commission is a matter of judicial discretion, but the circumstances in which a witness instead of being produced in Court, is sought to be examined on commission, should be carefully considered. Such commission should be issued on the ground of necessity and not as a matter of mere indulgence to one of the parties or for the mutual convenience of the parties. " He also relied on a decision reported he A.I.R. 1950 (Cal), 173, (Sris Chandra Nandy Vs. Sm. Annapuma Ray) wherein, it has been held that "Medical certificate tendered in support of an application for the issue of a commission for the examination of a witness on the ground of illness is inadmissible in evidence being the worst form of hearsay evidence. The doctor himself should be called in evidence." 

 17. This statement of the petitioner in review application clearly indicates and proves t at e predecessor-in-interest of the present petitioners was ill and no other interpretation can be given to these lines mentioned by the opposite party in their petition for review. It also clearly indicates that the opposite parties were fully aware of the illness of the original plaintiff. Under Order 47, rule I of the code of Civil Procedure new and important matter should be brought to the notice of the Court after due diligence which was not within his knowledge or could not be produced by him when the order was made. Admittedly the petition for appointing commissioner was made on 13.9.84 and the copy of the same was served upon the lawyer of the opposite party. But no objection was raised by the learned Advocate on behalf of the opposite party and he never sought any adjournment for giving objection or to get instruction from his client. After the aforesaid statement made in the petition for review on the illness of the plaintiff it cannot be said that the opposite party was not aware of the fact of the illness of the original plaintiff on 13.9.84. This admission on the part of the opposite party in their application for review belied their claim that important fact which was not known to them on 13.9.84 was discovered after due diligence. The person seeking relief under Order 47 rule I should prove certain materials i.e. 'the discovery of new and important matter which 'was not within his knowledge when the order under review' was made and when there is sufficient proof of the matter the review application should be allowed. Here in the present application it cannot be found that the opposite parties were not aware of the illness or otherwise of the original plaintiff on the date when the petition for commission was filed. The learned Advocate for the opposite party relief on certain decisions reported in 38 D.L.R. 47, 35 D.L.R. 461 and A.I.R. 1950(Cal) 178. These decisions were given by Hon'ble Courts in exercise of their revisional power under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The facts leading to these decisions are that the Courts below ordered for recording the evidence on commission against which revisional applications were filed and in those revisional applications it was found that in such cases the higher courts had every right to look into the propriety and legality of the order. These decisions were not in connection with the case filed under order 47, rule 1 of the Code and in that view of the matter I hold that the decisions cited by Mr. Abdul Kuddus Miah, the learned Advocate for the opposite party has no manner of application in the present case. The present case arose out of an application filed under Order 47, rule 1 C.P.C. and it must be decided in accordance with the provisions of this law.
